steps: A reader begins with a snapshot that sees version 3.
A concurrent writer creates and commits version 4 rather than overwriting v3 in place.
New readers see v4 while the original reader still sees v3.
Garbage collection removes v3 only after no active snapshot needs it.

lesson.scenario: A library catalog lets a long report read book availability while a checkout creates a newer row version.

steps.title: Pin a read snapshot
steps.narration: The report starts at timestamp 40 and sees BK-10 version 38 as available.
steps.outcome: The report has a stable visibility boundary.
steps.invariant: A reader sees the newest committed version not newer than its snapshot.

steps.title: Create instead of overwrite
steps.narration: Checkout transaction 42 writes a private BK-10 version while v38 remains intact.
steps.outcome: Readers and the writer coexist without in-place overwrite.
steps.invariant: Uncommitted versions are invisible to other transactions.

steps.title: Commit the new version
steps.narration: The checkout commits version 43 with borrower Maya.
steps.outcome: New transactions see v43 while the report still sees v38.
steps.invariant: Commit adds a visibility interval; it does not rewrite an older snapshot.

steps.title: Preserve repeatable reading
steps.narration: The report rereads BK-10 and still receives v38 because timestamp 43 is in its future.
steps.outcome: The long report is internally consistent without blocking checkout.
steps.invariant: Visibility is determined by version timestamps and transaction ownership.

steps.title: Reclaim after snapshot release
steps.narration: When the report ends, no active snapshot needs v38 and vacuum removes it.
steps.outcome: Storage is recovered only after visibility safety permits it.
steps.invariant: Vacuum never removes a version visible to any active snapshot.

production.scenario: A seller catalog dashboard keeps long reads stable while a bulk import continuously publishes new prices and inventory.
components: Merchandisers browsing the live catalog and inventory state
Boundary service that serves filtered catalog views
Black-box transaction manager that gives readers a stable view of catalog rows
Authoritative products, prices, inventory, and change history
Publishes new price files and inventory corrections
Rebuilds replicas or restores the catalog after storage incidents
Advances cleanup policy for obsolete row versions
flows: A merchandiser asks for a filtered catalog or inventory view.
The API opens one stable read view for the user session before scanning catalog rows.
Only row versions visible to that read view are returned from the authoritative database.
Bulk imports write new price and inventory versions without blocking readers already in flight.
The primary database feeds the restore worker with the data needed for point-in-time recovery.
Recovery can reseed a replica or restore the primary to a requested point in time.
A control path periodically permits old catalog versions to be removed once reads no longer need them.
